proposals.evidence: CDIAL 1670 ujjvala explicitly gives Maithili ujjar/ujar “white” and notes Bihar-to-Nepali transmission; the survey forms fit this family. Comparative check: MagahiNepal ūjjar “white” (f_jq4ugx46zqzfc). The exact survey spelling and phonetic marks remain untouched. Stress, vowel articulation, release marks and source palatal/sibilant notation were reviewed as local details; the full form and sense support the same family. The link does not settle uncertain transfer within Indo-Aryan.
